title: Minucher v. Court of Appeals
summary: The Supreme Court ruled on the scope of diplomatic immunity, holding that a US Drug Enforcement Administration agent was immune from suit for acts performed in the course of his official duties. State immunity from suit extends to agents acting within the scope of their authority.
doctrine: Foreign agents performing acts within the scope of their official duties are immune from suit under the doctrine of state immunity. The immunity extends not only to the foreign state itself but to its agents and instrumentalities. The test is whether the act was performed in the discharge of official functions.
fullText:
VITUG, J.:

The central issue is whether a US Drug Enforcement Administration agent is immune from suit for acts performed in the course of his official duties in the Philippines.

The doctrine of state immunity provides that a sovereign state cannot be sued without its consent. This immunity extends to agents and instrumentalities of the foreign state when they act within the scope of their authority.

The test for determining whether a suit against a government agent is in fact a suit against the state is whether the ultimate liability will fall on the government. If the agent performed the act in the discharge of official functions, the suit is essentially one against the state and must be dismissed.
